question: If at same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is ₹42 and compound interest is ₹43, then what is the principal (in ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI is simply the interest earned on the 1st year's simple interest.

1st year's SI = ₹42 ÷ 2 = ₹21.

Difference = ₹43 − ₹42 = ₹1 (This is the interest earned on ₹21 in the 2nd year).

Rate (R) = (Interest ÷ Principal) × 100 = (1 ÷ 21) × 100%.

Principal = (1st year's SI × 100) ÷ R = (21 × 100) ÷ (100/21) = 21 × 21 = ₹441.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹441.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

SI for 2 years = ₹42

CI for 2 years = ₹43

Time = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Difference for 2 years = CI − SI = Interest generated on the 1st year's SI

 
 Principal (P) = ?

 
• 
 
• 

 
 1st Yr SI = ₹21

 
 2nd Yr SI = ₹21

 
• 
 Rate R%

 
 Diff (on 1st SI) = ₹1

 Total SI = ₹42
 Total CI = ₹43

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI is the same for every year, so 1st year's SI = 42 ÷ 2 = ₹21

⇒ CI for the 2nd year = Total CI − 1st year's SI = 43 − 21 = ₹22

⇒ Extra interest generated in the 2nd year = CI for 2nd year − SI for 2nd year = 22 − 21 = ₹1

⇒ This ₹1 is the simple interest calculated on the 1st year's SI (₹21) for a period of 1 year.

⇒ Rate (R) = (100 × Interest) ÷ (Principal × Time)

⇒ R = (100 × 1) ÷ (21 × 1) = 100/21%

⇒ Now, substitute R into the SI formula for the 1st year:

⇒ 21 = (P × (100/21) × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ 21 = P ÷ 21

⇒ P = 21 × 21

⇒ P = ₹441

**∴ The correct answer is ₹441.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI (2 Years)

The formula is Diff = P × (R/100)². It strictly represents the interest generated on the first year's simple interest.

Difference between CI and SI (3 Years)

The formula is Diff = P × (R/100)² × (3 + R/100). This formula helps bypass lengthy calculations for 3-year differences.

Uniformity of Simple Interest

Simple Interest (SI) is calculated only on the original principal. Therefore, the interest earned remains constant for every year of the investment period.
